claims.text: Initially solid Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are the system under study.
Standard rapid synthesis produces inherent defect densities in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles.
Rapid synthesis produces slight local compositional fluctuations in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles.
Post-synthesis thermal annealing reduces nanoparticle defect density.
Post-synthesis thermal annealing homogenizes the local elemental distribution.
Internal lattice strain and local compositional heterogeneity are the primary mediators of premelting and melting in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles.
Synthesis-induced defects cause the relevant lattice strain and local compositional heterogeneity.
Defect-rich or locally segregated regions have lower local cohesive energy.
The reduced cohesive energy of defect-rich or segregated regions lowers their local melting point relative to the rest of the particle.
Locally reduced melting points initiate premelting at defect-rich or segregated sites.
Spatial variation in local melting points broadens the overall melting transition.
Annealed, defect-reduced nanoparticles will exhibit a higher and more uniform melting onset than untreated nanoparticles.
Annealed, compositionally more uniform nanoparticles will exhibit a sharper melting transition than untreated nanoparticles.
Untreated defect-rich nanoparticles will premelt at lower temperatures and over a wider temperature range.
Reducing defects and compositional heterogeneity will move melting closer to the expected bulk melting temperature.
The proposed mechanism applies to chemically similar high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles approximately 5–50 nm in size when surface and defect-mediated premelting effects are significant.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to larger-scale materials or to particles synthesized without defects.
Surface-energy effects may contribute to premelting independently of internal defects.
XRD peak shifts or broadening can be used as evidence for the onset of premelting in this experiment.
No statistically significant change in melting onset or transition width after confirmed defect reduction would falsify the claim that defects and compositional heterogeneity are the key drivers.
